name: pulse-filetree
description: An IDE-style file tree for Claude Code that shows what Claude is doing and where in files

activity.title: Claude activity
activity.description: Which of Claude's file activity shimmers in the tree: files read with the Read tool or Bash readers (rg, grep, find, cat) in purple, writes in orange, git actions in green and a subagent's reads and writes in lilac. The same setting decides which touches outside the folder are listed under the tree and whether deleted files stay as faded rows.

glyphs.title: Glyphs
glyphs.description: Icon set: auto uses Nerd Font icons when one is installed here, Lucide icons in the desktop app, and otherwise coloured type badges (TS, JS, {}) and coloured folders; nerd forces Nerd Font icons in the terminal; plain forces the badges everywhere

follow.title: Follow Claude
follow.description: on: the tree scrolls to what Claude reads, writes or commits. off: the view stays where you put it and only your own scrolling moves it; highlights still show.

start.title: Open at start
start.description: on: the pane opens when a session starts. In the terminal it needs the fullscreen layout and at least 110 columns, as /filetree does; with less it stays closed and a toast says why. off: it stays closed until you run /filetree.

column.title: Right column
column.description: What the right column shows by default: date (last modified), age (time since last modified, short: now, 12m, 3h, 5d, then Oct 9 past a week and the year past a year) or size (files in bytes, folders as disk usage computed in the background). The header button toggles between size and the date or age, and s in the tree cycles date, age and size.

hints.title: Hints
hints.description: on: outside a git repo, a line under the header says git status starts after git init. off: the line is hidden and the tree gets the row.

open.title: Open with
open.description: What a double-click or Enter does with a file. Empty: the default app. preview: show it in the pane (left goes back). Anything else is a command run instead: {path} is the file and {dir} its folder; without {path} the path goes last. Words split on spaces, quotes keep a word whole, and no shell runs it. It should start the viewer and return; on Linux it runs detached.
